qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Iconic century-old confectionery brands (Reese's, Hershey's, Kisses, Kit Kat US license) command ~45% US chocolate confectionery market share and entrenched checkout-lane front-end shelf placement that competitors cannot economically displace. Proven pricing power with multi-year high single-digit price realizations absorbing historic cocoa shocks; 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 21.2% well above the 12% hurdle. Primary erosion threats include GLP-1 weight-loss adoption reducing impulse snacking, extreme raw cocoa input volatility, and retailer private-label encroachment in salty snacks.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates into funnel. Dominant US confectionery franchise with ~45% chocolate market share and iconic Lindy brands (Reese's, Hershey's, Kisses). Strong pricing power has consistently countered severe agricultural cost shocks. Balance sheet remains conservative with net debt/EBITDA ~2.0x, interest coverage >7.5x even at cyclical cocoa troughs, and FCF conversion >100%. [5-10Y g: snack volume 1.0% + brand pricing 2.0% + product mix 1.0% - input cost drag 0.5% + share repurchases 1.5%]
qualitative.evidence: 10-year average ROIC exceeds 20% (5-year median GAAP ROIC ~21.2%), remaining resilient through economic cycles and troughing near ~10% only during unprecedented 2024-2025 cocoa commodity spikes. Operating cash flow of $1.7B-$1.9B reliably generates FCF conversion >100% of net income ($1.7B-$1.9B FCF vs $1.1B-$1.8B NI). FY2025 operating income of $1.44B covers net interest expense of $190M by 7.6x (17.5x in FY2024), and net debt (~$3.6B) is repayable in ~2.0 years of normal owner earnings. Reese's remains the #1 confection brand in the US, supporting dominant front-end retail checkout placement and category-leading gross margins.
